talking-heads>velvet-underground.found: No surprise I was a big fan, and his music, with and without the Velvets, was a big influence on myself and Talking Heads.
talking-heads>velvet-underground.citation: David Byrne to Rolling Stone on Lou Reed's death (2013): "his music, with and without the Velvets, was a big influence on myself and Talking Heads." He added: "His work and that of the Velvets was a big reason I moved to NY."
talking-heads>velvet-underground.note: Original quote 'a big reason I moved to New York' was a mangled join of two sentences; page says 'a big reason I moved to NY'. Not a 'tribute' piece but Byrne's statement to Rolling Stone.

brian-eno>velvet-underground.found: I think everyone who bought one of those 30,000 copies started a band!
brian-eno>velvet-underground.note: Quote Investigator reproduces the 23 May 1982 Los Angeles Times piece (Kristine McKenna, 'Lots of Aura, No Air Play', p. L6) with the line; original is ProQuest only. Eno is the speaker. (McKenna has said elsewhere it ran in Musician; QI cites the LA Times.)

mogwai>nick-drake.found: It’s a perfect record. Succinct, sad, melodic, definitely its own thing. The simplicity of it was a big thing for me, that music that simple can also be really moving
mogwai>nick-drake.note: Quietus Baker's Dozen, item 13 Nick Drake Pink Moon; Braithwaite speaking. Opened via r.jina.ai.

radiohead>rem.found: Then I discovered R.E.M. and it turned my life upside down.
radiohead>rem.citation: Thom Yorke to VinylWriters, as quoted by Far Out: "Then I discovered R.E.M. and it turned my life upside down." He added: "Shortly after that, I signed up for art school and started to take making music seriously."
radiohead>rem.note: Original quote elided 'that' in 'Shortly after that'; caption line replaced with the cleaner 'turned my life upside down' sentence. Far Out names VinylWriters as the original; original not opened.

my-bloody-valentine>sonic-youth.note: Named the outlet/year; Shields is the speaker.

the-cure>david-bowie.found: David Bowie was probably the first artist that I felt was mine. He was singing to me.
the-cure>david-bowie.citation: Robert Smith, asked how Bowie influenced his approach to music, as quoted by Far Out: "David Bowie was probably the first artist that I felt was mine. He was singing to me." Ziggy Stardust was the first vinyl album he bought.
the-cure>david-bowie.note: The 'David Bowie was an obvious influence on me' line was not found on this page, in Wikipedia's Cure/Robert Smith pages, or in one search; replaced with a verbatim line from the same Smith answer. Far Out gives no original outlet for the clip. 'first vinyl album I ever bought' is on the page as: _Ziggy Stardust_ was the first vinyl album I ever bought.

slowdive>my-bloody-valentine.found: When I listened to My Bloody Valentine and Cocteau Twins I wanted something between those sounds.
slowdive>my-bloody-valentine.citation: Neil Halstead to Reverb (2017): "When I listened to My Bloody Valentine and Cocteau Twins I wanted something between those sounds."
slowdive>my-bloody-valentine.note: Quote verbatim on the Reverb interview (published 2017-06-16, Halstead and Christian Savill). The paragraph carries no speaker label but follows Halstead's labelled answers on tunings/reverb, so attributed to him. The claim in the old citation that Goswell and Savill 'said the same in separate interviews' was not verified and is dropped. Resolves the project's note that this Halstead quote had no source.

slowdive>pixies.note: Under the Radar, 'Slowdive - Neil Halstead and Rachel Goswell on the bands that inspired them' (2014). Search summary says it carries Goswell: "We really liked Pixies. Doolittle was kind of an anthemic LP for us back in those days." Cloudflare wall blocks read, archive.org copy and WebFetch (403). Look for that quote, and that Goswell is the speaker.

nirvana>wipers.found: The first two [albums] were totally classic and influenced the Melvins and all the other punk rock bands. They’re another band I tried to assimilate,
nirvana>wipers.citation: Kurt Cobain to Melody Maker, on the Wipers: "The first two [albums] were totally classic and influenced the Melvins and all the other punk rock bands. They're another band I tried to assimilate."
nirvana>wipers.note: Verbatim on two Far Out pieces (which name Melody Maker as the original; original not opened). Far Out prints 'The first two [albums]', the bracket being an editor's gloss; kept in the citation. The 'named three records among favourites' part of the old citation was not checked here and is dropped.

rem>big-star.note: Two searches (exact quote; Buck + Big Star + 'as popular'); no page carries 'I was hoping we might get as popular as Big Star.' Related line that IS sourced: Wikipedia's Big Star page quotes Peter Buck: "We've sort of flirted with greatness, but we've yet to make a record as good as Revolver or Highway 61 Revisited or Exile on Main Street or Big Star's Third." (footnote is a book, Jovanovic p.247 per the rp tag) - an admiration/comparison, not a hope to be as popular; could replace the caption if the owner wants it.

ride>the-smiths.found: Still, I didn't think about it too much until I heard the Smiths on the radio when I was 13, in 1983. I really, really liked the sound of the band, so I went and bought the first cassette of theirs I could find. That's when it all clicked. I was immediately trying to figure out Johnny Marr's guitar parts.
ride>the-smiths.citation: Andy Bell to Premier Guitar: "I heard the Smiths on the radio when I was 13, in 1983. I really, really liked the sound of the band, so I went and bought the first cassette of theirs I could find. That's when it all clicked. I was immediately trying to figure out Johnny Marr's guitar parts."
ride>the-smiths.note: The VWMusic line ('By age thirteen, I was getting into The Smiths, and Johnny Marr was a big formative influence') was not found (one search, no hit); replaced with Bell's own words from Premier Guitar. Guitar.com 'Ride Revival' also has Bell: 'When The Smiths came out, I was still a bit young, I was 13 and obsessed with Johnny Marr and a bit of a copyist.' found text is as printed (straight apostrophes).

dinosaur-jr>the-birthday-party.found: Dinosaur was really influenced by Neil Young and Black Sabbath and also a lot of... not exactly indie rock, since that wasn't around then. There was stuff like the Birthday Party, Scratch Acid and Sonic Youth.
dinosaur-jr>the-birthday-party.citation: Lou Barlow to Jason Gross in Perfect Sound Forever (January 1997): "There was stuff like the Birthday Party, Scratch Acid and Sonic Youth." Of Dinosaur Jr., he said they were "really influenced by Neil Young and Black Sabbath".
dinosaur-jr>the-birthday-party.note: 'we were into The Birthday Party' and Mascis breaking eggs for Cave's haircut were not found (Village Voice Barlow Q&A via archive.org has neither). Replaced with Barlow's words in PSF. Barlow is speaking about Dinosaur (his old band) in general, third person, so first-person tier is a stretch but he was a member; keep as first-person or lower to reported - owner's call. Wikipedia Dinosaur Jr. also says Mascis frequently names Nick Cave as an influence (unsourced here).

dinosaur-jr>wipers.note: Guitar World's '10 guitarists who shaped my sound' text could not be opened or found (listing page only; BrooklynVegan says Greg Sage is on the list); replaced with Mascis's 'Foundations' answer in Clash (page published 2014-07-08), Over the Edge entry.
